chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Yazeed ibn Hatim, who said:

There was a spy for Abdul Malik ibn Marwan in Medina who used to write to him with the news of whatever transpired therein, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) emancipated a slave girl, then married her. So the spy wrote to Abdul Malik, and Abdul Malik wrote to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Thereafter, it has reached me that you married your slave girl, and you know that there are matches for you from Qureysh, one you can glorify with regarding the relationship and have excellence regarding the children, but you did not consider for yourself nor upon your children to remain. Greetings!'

So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Thereafter, your letter has reached me, chiding me due to my marrying my slave girl, and you alleged that there are women among Qureysh ones I can glorify with regarding the relationship, and have excellence regarding the children, and there is no higher level than that of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with regards to glory, nor any more in benevolence. But rather, she was a possession of my right hand. When Allah (Mighty and Majestic) Intended a matter from me, I sought His Rewards by it. Then I returned her upon a Sunnah. And whoever was pure in the Religion of Allah, so there is nothing which can isolate him from His Command, and Allah has Raised by Al-Islam the despicability and completed the short-comings with it, and removed the blames. Thus, there is no blame upon a Muslim person, but rather the blame is upon the ignorance. Greetings!'

So when he read the letter, he threw it to his son Suleyman, so he read it, and he said, 'O commander of the faithful! How intense is what Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) has prided over you!' So he said, 'O my son! Do not say that, for it is the tongues of the Clan of Hashim (peace be upon him) which splits the rocks and scoops from an ocean. It is Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), O my son, who rises from where the people are humbled'.
ai.seo_question: What was Ali ibn al-Husayn's response to Abdul Malik's criticism of his marriage to a freed slave girl?
ai.summary: This epistolary exchange highlights the theological clash between Umayyad tribal elitism and the Shia emphasis on spiritual meritocracy, where Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) asserts that Islam elevates the humble and nullifies pre-Islamic lineage pride. The narrative concludes with Sulayman ibn Abdul Malik’s recognition of Zayn al-Abidin’s eloquence and spiritual depth, illustrating the concept of 'rising from where people humble themselves' as a mark of true nobility in Shia tradition.
